title.title: Fontaine–Mazur at the prime 2, with no residual hypothesis
title.subtitle: Claim: every odd, de Rham, 2-dimensional 2-adic Galois representation of $\mathbb{Q}$ is modular

beats.text: Fontaine–Mazur: a geometric 2-dimensional Galois representation comes from a modular form
At $p = 2$, scalar and reducible residual images $\bar r$ were the open cases
It is also the modularity input to the Hilbert's tenth claim, family 004

achievement.label: Fontaine–Mazur conjecture (1995), odd regular case over Q
statement: r: G_{\mathbb{Q}} \to \mathrm{GL}_2(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_2) \text{ odd, de Rham} \Rightarrow r \text{ modular}
achievement.context: Before at $p = 2$: solvable (Allen 2016) and nonsolvable (Tung 2021) residual images only
achievement.note: With distinct Hodge–Tate weights: a Tate twist of a classical eigenform

verify.detail: No Lean; 113 pages over three papers, and family 004 inherits the risk
verify.ourCheck: We read the main theorem and caveats; nothing was checked independently

sources.quote: At p = 2: Allen (2016) solvable residual image nearly ordinary; Tung (2021) nonsolvable residual image. Globally scalar or reducible residual image at 2 remained open.
At odd p: Kisin (2009) and Emerton (2011) under residual hypotheses
At odd primes this was essentially done (Kisin, Emerton, Pan, and a last case at 3)
if moreover r is de Rham at 2 with distinct Hodge-Tate weights it is a Tate twist of the 2-adic representation of a classical cuspidal eigenform
Not formalized; 113 pages over three papers. The Fontaine-Mazur paper says it supplies the weight-two modularity input for the Hilbert-tenth-over-Q proof (family 004), so H10 inherits its risk.
read each family's summary and abstracts and the introduction and main theorem of every principal paper

plain: Certain symmetries of the rational numbers were predicted to come from modular forms; this settles the prime 2

steps: Start with a 2-adic symmetry of the rational numbers
First show it appears in a big space of modular objects
Then show it is a genuine classical modular form

voice.text: Odd primes were essentially done. At two, scalar and reducible cases stayed open.
First it appears in completed cohomology, then it becomes a classical form.
Claimed: every such representation is modular.
